To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a rule-based approach to view updating can be based on rule transformations performed in schema design and that (2) fixpoint computations of these rules can be used at run time to realize view update requests.

- the approach is based on rule transformations, - it uses fixpoint computations, - it supports stratifiably recursive views, - it allows for alternative realizations of update requests, and - it can be implemented efficiently.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: - Transformation of Datalog rules into a more efficient form.
a new approach for consistency preserving update in deductive databases based on rule transformations performed in schema design and fixpoint computations performed during run time.
the following questions: How can we efficiently update views in deductive databases in such a way that consistency is preserved?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach is a good compromise between the two extremes of the spectrum: on the one hand it is based on a sound theoretical foundation (the fixpoint semantics of stratifiably recursive Datalog programs) and on the other hand it provides an efficient implementation.
the approach is a promising basis for further research in this area.
the approach presented in the paper is a good example of how to integrate the two most prominent approaches for deductive databases (the rule-based and the logic-based one).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented approach is a new way to integrate the well-known techniques for efficient query and integrity checking in a rule-based approach for view updating.
we have shown how a transformation-based view updating approach for Datalog can be extended to the case of stratifiable Datalog programs with recursive view definitions.
we have presented a new, efficient and flexible approach to view update processing that is based on rule transformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rule transformation techniques used in the context of query answering and integrity maintenance are applicable in the context of view update, too.
the use of transformation techniques for rule-based view updating is feasible, even for complex, recursive views.
rule transformations, which are usually considered as schema design issues, can also be used to improve the performance of run-time operations like view updating.
